beats.spoken: Four stores hold one task's state today, joined by two orchestrators that poll each other.

visual.assertion: One task, four stores, two orchestrators

beats.spoken: The tick counted a hundred and forty-three claims when about sixty were real. A finished report can wait up to thirteen minutes to be seen.

visual.assertion: Seams between stores show up as errors

beats.spoken: The backlog holds the task file. The burndown tick keeps a ledger, and the broker keeps a roster of agents.

visual.assertion: Each part keeps its own store

chips.text: hand layout of the factory maps

beats.spoken: An implementer opens a pull request for Shepherd, which keeps a fourth store and merges to main.

visual.assertion: Shepherd keeps a fourth store

chips.text: hand layout of the factory maps

beats.spoken: Around them: a reviewer, a coordinator seat, and you. Shepherd's asks for reviewers time out in batches, and the tick re-registers pull requests as a backstop.

visual.assertion: Every seam needs a patch

chips.text: hand layout of the factory maps

beats.spoken: One thousand six hundred and twenty-six messages went to the seat. In two weeks, three hundred and thirteen held fix rounds waited on a hand resume.

visual.assertion: The seat patches seams by hand

beats.spoken: The redesign keeps, removes and adds parts, and leaves eleven calls to you.

visual.assertion: Keeps, removes, adds, and your calls

beats.spoken: Seven jobs come first: choose, make and prove. Then land, keep going, ask the owner, and stay legible.

visual.assertion: Seven jobs any factory must do

beats.spoken: CI passes on the merged tree; a verdict counts only at its exact head; authority and security get stronger review. Caps hold, no agent widens its permissions, stalls heal unaided, and state survives restarts.

visual.assertion: Seven invariants hold whatever the mechanism

beats.spoken: No webhooks reach this box, CI has twenty runners, agents crash, you want to be asked rarely.

visual.assertion: Four limits the design cannot change

beats.spoken: Twenty mechanisms exist only to patch others. The design aims for under five, with one clock and one store.

visual.assertion: Twenty patches today; the aim is under five

cues.target: chip:aim: under five, one clock, one store

beats.spoken: Seven nouns carry the new model. Item, fact and step; wait and claim; event, pool and service.

visual.assertion: Seven nouns carry the whole model

beats.spoken: One sentence explains it. A recipe is a script, a step is memoized at its head, a wait or claim is a return, and an event re-enters the script.

visual.assertion: Script, memo, return, re-entry

contested.fallback: One sentence explains it. A recipe is a script, each step leaves a memoized marker, a wait or claim is a return, and an event re-enters the script.
contested.why: Review-type facts may key by diff digest, not head; R-D §0 item 3: reads of holds, policy, roster and mergeability change without a head move

beats.spoken: On the new map, backlog and broker keep their places. Plans carry a contract for every slice.

visual.assertion: Backlog and broker stay put; plans gain contracts

chips.text: hand layout of the factory maps

beats.spoken: One runner and its marker table replace the tick and Shepherd. It re-runs a recipe on every event; its only clock, the reconciler, polls GitHub.

visual.assertion: One runner replaces tick and Shepherd

chips.text: hand layout of the factory maps

beats.spoken: The broker becomes a runtime that spawns short-lived agents. Agents push to GitHub, and a merge queue lands the work.

visual.assertion: The broker becomes a runtime

chips.text: hand layout of the factory maps

beats.spoken: Main stays put, and so do you, reading packets in a console. Alarms go to ops, not you.

visual.assertion: Main and owner stay; alarms go elsewhere

chips.text: hand layout of the factory maps

beats.spoken: Pool policy details, risk table rows and stacking are left out; each is data, so the shape holds.

visual.assertion: Tables, policies and plans hold the details

beats.spoken: A recipe is a plain script; here are five of its steps. Each step runs, writes a marker for its fact, and returns. A landed run averages fifty-one and a half steps.

visual.assertion: A recipe is a script of steps

beats.spoken: Halfway through the fifth step, the process crashes. No program counter is stored, and nothing was mid-sleep.

visual.assertion: A crash leaves only the markers

beats.spoken: Recovery re-runs the script from the top. Four markers match, so it fast-forwards and runs the fifth step.

visual.assertion: Recovery is a re-run from the top

beats.spoken: Today's engine keys each result by step name and call count. When a deploy re-keyed one step, its old results went unread, and five parked runs failed to replay.

visual.assertion: Today a re-keyed step strands its results

beats.spoken: Keyed by fact, an inserted step has no marker, so it runs, and the old markers still match.

visual.assertion: An inserted step runs; old markers match

contested.fallback: Keyed by fact, an inserted step has no marker, so it runs, and the old markers still match. Inserts ahead of a landing are still under review.
contested.why: 'Inserting a step is safe' overclaims for a gate ahead of an intent marker, ordering-sensitive effects and reads that change a branch

beats.spoken: Change an upstream step, and the markers that read it go stale. The next entry re-runs only those.

visual.assertion: A changed step re-runs what read it

contested.fallback: Change an upstream step, and the design marks the markers that read it stale; the next entry re-runs them. How far a change reaches is under review.
contested.why: The version lint is per file, so a rule-file or helper change leaves gating markers valid; bumps need a scope

beats.spoken: A claim is a marker too. If the plan changes after the grant, the grant goes stale and releases its token before anything re-runs.

visual.assertion: A stale grant gives its token back first

contested.fallback: A claim is a marker too. If what it read changes, the design releases the grant's token before anything re-runs. When grants are checked is under review.
contested.why: Item facts such as contract:approved never go stale, and a grant is re-checked only on re-entry

beats.spoken: So how does one task reach main?

visual.assertion: The shape at rest; now one task

chips.text: hand layout of the factory maps

beats.spoken: A planner splits it into slices with contracts: risk class, requirements, the change in one sentence, exclusive paths. You approve them in one plan sitting.

visual.assertion: Every slice carries a contract you approve

chips.text: hand layout of the factory maps

beats.spoken: The recipe claims an implementer and returns. The pool picks which claim to grant, not the item, and the broker spawns the agent.

visual.assertion: The pool picks which claim to grant

chips.text: hand layout of the factory maps

beats.spoken: Its push opens a pull request. The runner records the head, and the facts it still needs appear as chips. Path globs can raise its class.

visual.assertion: A push records the head

chips.text: hand layout of the factory maps

beats.spoken: CI goes green and the proof reproduces. The verdict is a claim on the reviewer pool, and a short-lived reviewer returns merge.

visual.assertion: Facts turn green at this head

chips.text: hand layout of the factory maps

beats.spoken: That reviewer saw a security touch and raised the class, adding an adversary review on another profile or account. Nobody can lower a class.

visual.assertion: A class can rise, never fall

chips.text: hand layout of the factory maps

beats.spoken: A red fact wakes the implementer at once. Its push moves the head and resets every head-pinned chip.

visual.assertion: A push resets every head-pinned chip

chips.text: hand layout of the factory maps

beats.spoken: You are asked only if the class says so, at a settled head. An agent writes the packet, which cancels if the head moves before delivery.

visual.assertion: You are asked once, at a settled head

chips.text: hand layout of the factory maps

beats.spoken: Once it reaches you, fixes wait for your answer. A rule file asks live only for a looser or mixed change, the authority table, or a ruleset.

visual.assertion: Rule files ask live only when looser

chips.text: hand layout of the factory maps

beats.spoken: With every chip green, the merge queue tests main plus ready heads as one candidate. It writes an intent marker, lands main at that tree, then writes the result.

visual.assertion: Landing writes intent, then result

chips.text: hand layout of the factory maps

beats.spoken: The head never moves. Main's CI confirms, and a red main gets one fixer from the tip. The last slice to land closes the task.

visual.assertion: The head never moves; main confirms

chips.text: hand layout of the factory maps

beats.spoken: A stalled item's lease expires. After three re-drives, a triager picks one fixed verdict: restart, file a defect and park, or escalate to ops.

visual.assertion: Stalls end in a fixed verdict

chips.text: hand layout of the factory maps

beats.spoken: Side by side: hold slots, each class with its own release, become one requirement set per head.

visual.assertion: Hold slots become per-head requirements

chips.text: hand layout of the factory maps

beats.spoken: Merge-ups move the reviewed head on thirty to thirty-five percent of heads, about a quarter of runner minutes. The queue's candidate leaves heads alone.

visual.assertion: Merge-ups move heads; the queue does not

chips.text: hand layout of the factory maps

beats.spoken: A six-hundred-second tick becomes events, with the poller as a backstop.

visual.assertion: A timer becomes events plus a backstop

chips.text: hand layout of the factory maps

beats.spoken: Seat release becomes software in steps: deny-only guard changes on conformance, other adversary classes only after the F7 eval.

visual.assertion: Software releases only after its eval

chips.text: hand layout of the factory maps

beats.spoken: Ask-and-wait reviews become a pull queue, red-main fixes first.

visual.assertion: Ask-and-wait becomes a pull queue

chips.text: hand layout of the factory maps

beats.spoken: Of seven hundred seventeen owner gates in seven days, four hundred eighty-two were cancelled, three hundred and two because the head moved. Now one class asks, at a settled head.

visual.assertion: Most owner gates resolved without you

chips.text: hand layout of the factory maps

beats.spoken: Seat work goes to the scheduler and the triager, and a seat becomes a partition you switch. Lead-desk becomes the ops alarm sink.

visual.assertion: Seat work moves into software

chips.text: hand layout of the factory maps

beats.spoken: The planner's contract sets the class floor, and the implementer can only raise it.

visual.assertion: The plan sets the class floor

chips.text: hand layout of the factory maps

beats.spoken: You move to the plan sitting, and to the console for expedites and looser or mixed packets.

visual.assertion: Your work moves to plan time

chips.text: hand layout of the factory maps

beats.spoken: Shepherd's steps become registered steps, burndown becomes a recipe, and agent-chat becomes a runtime.

visual.assertion: Steps register; burndown becomes a recipe

chips.text: hand layout of the factory maps

beats.spoken: Seven carry modules and the three forty-one stopgap go at rung three, safe because the queue never moves a head.

visual.assertion: Carry modules go: heads never move

beats.spoken: Hold slots give way to per-head requirements. The no-reviewer hold and defect gates give way to leases, re-drives and the triager.

visual.assertion: Holds and defect gates give way to leases

beats.spoken: Role caps give way to pools and three hard stops: the five-hour ceiling, the seven-day reserve line, and the per-run cap.

visual.assertion: Pools and three hard stops replace caps

beats.spoken: Notices go: almost no park refusal was acted on. The file lock goes after F12, and no coordinator stays in the loop.

visual.assertion: Notices, the file lock and coordinator go

beats.spoken: The weighted score goes. Two pool rules replace it: finish before start, then tier and readiness age.

visual.assertion: Two pool rules replace the score

beats.spoken: Replay keyed by step name and call count goes. Markers are keyed by fact instead; a run-wide counter key is what parked five runs.

visual.assertion: Counter-keyed replay goes

beats.spoken: The adversary converged with no blocking objection, but kept three risks. First, an agent labels rule-file changes no checker covers, so a disguised loosening could skip your live ask. The adversary must still approve.

visual.assertion: Converged, with three risks on record

beats.spoken: Second, big gains wait on follow-ups; F7 must price the seat's hand catches. Third, two orchestrators remain until rung eight.

visual.assertion: Gains wait on tests; two orchestrators remain

beats.spoken: Eighteen additions build it, in twelve groups. First the core: the marker table, the step registry and the runner, then waits and events.

visual.assertion: Eighteen additions; the runner's core comes first

chips.text: hand layout of the factory maps

beats.spoken: Claims and pools gate every spawn. An outbox guards each land and deploy, against the bug behind two deploy rollbacks. A reconciler reads GitHub.

visual.assertion: Claims, an outbox and a reconciler

chips.text: hand layout of the factory maps

beats.spoken: Plans gain a contract and the risk table. A review pool and the merge queue prove and land the work. Packets, a triager and alarms handle the rest.

visual.assertion: Contracts, review pool, queue, packets, alarms

chips.text: hand layout of the factory maps

beats.spoken: Last come why, the restart pacer, evals and invariant tests, and your expedite entry.

visual.assertion: why, a pacer, tests and your expedite

chips.text: hand layout of the factory maps

beats.spoken: It ships as eleven rungs, each behind a flag or in shadow, naming what it deletes.

visual.assertion: Eleven rungs, each reversible by a flag

beats.spoken: Rung zero fixes data honesty, one shadows requirements and ships why, two adds the review queue, and three the merge queue.

visual.assertion: Honest data, shadow, review queue, merge queue

beats.spoken: Four wakes fixers, five shadows the adversary, six requires contracts, seven folds owner gates into one class.

visual.assertion: Fixer wakes, adversary shadow, contracts, gates

beats.spoken: Eight moves dispatch into the factory after a forty-eight-hour shadow, reversibly, in parallel: about fifty-five agent-hours. Nine adds the restart pacer; ten shrinks the charter.

visual.assertion: Rung eight runs in parallel, reversibly

beats.spoken: Eleven calls are yours, none technical, each with a default.

visual.assertion: Eleven owner calls, each with a default

beats.spoken: First, landing per repo. Option a: the token bypasses the ruleset and main fast-forwards to the tested candidate. Option b: API merges, a tree-hash check, the up-to-date rule off.

visual.assertion: Q1: two ways to land, per repo

beats.spoken: Under a, CI holds by construction; under b, for each batch's final tree only. Unanswered, b applies where that rule is off; other repos wait.

visual.assertion: Q1: what each option guarantees

beats.spoken: Two to four: confirm the stopgap, adopt the rule-file review rule, and keep fixes waiting on a delivered packet. Each default is yes.

visual.assertion: Q2 to Q4 confirm earlier calls

cues.target: open:Q2 stopgap · build, delete at M3
open:Q4 fixes wait after a packet

beats.spoken: Five: which seat partitions run, by default lead-desk's alone. Six: a console expedite, by default added at rung eight.

visual.assertion: Q5 and Q6: seats and your expedite

beats.spoken: Seven: a blind sitting on real packets. Eight: a daily line, not alarms. Nine: a shadow run before a reversible cutover. The defaults: schedule, daily line, accept.

visual.assertion: Q7 to Q9: your time, alarms, cutover

beats.spoken: Ten: two pool rules replace the weighted score, tried in shadow first. Eleven: four researchers study the pattern first. Both defaults are yes.

visual.assertion: Q10 and Q11: pool rules and research

cues.target: open:Q10 pool rules for the score

beats.spoken: Eight follow-ups settle the technical forks, from F1's queue age to F13's landing test.

visual.assertion: Eight follow-ups settle the technical forks

beats.spoken: Research comes first: durable engines, build-system memoization, waits and claims, and an audit of our own engine, one researcher each.

visual.assertion: Four researchers report before the next round

beats.spoken: Measures: how fast why answers, how many asks are superseded, how many reviews end with no verdict. Latency has no target until F1.

visual.assertion: Three measures, and latency waits for F1

beats.spoken: In this design, a recipe is a script, each step leaves a marker, and recovery is a re-run from the top. Every wait names its reason. The open calls are yours.

visual.assertion: Every wait names its reason

chips.text: hand layout of the factory maps

beats.spoken: Find the wake, and you find the wait.

visual.assertion: Find the wake, find the wait

R01.claim: One task's state lives in four stores (task file, burndown.json, broker roster and events.db, factory.sqlite3); two orchestrators, the tick and Shepherd, join them by polling and calling each other's CLIs

R02.claim: The tick summary read `claimed` 143 against about 60 real claims

R03.claim: A DONE report is seen by the ledger up to 13 min late (tick period plus runtime)

R04.claim: Shepherd's reviewer asks time out in batches (ReviewerAskTimedOut); the roster read as their cause is inferred

R05.claim: 1,626 Shepherd-to-seat messages; 313 held fix rounds relayed for a hand resume in two weeks

R06.claim: The tick re-registers PRs with Shepherd as a backstop

R07.claim: Seven jobs: choose, make, prove, land, keep going, ask the owner, be legible

R08.claim: Seven invariants I1-I7; the mechanism is open, the invariant is not

R09.claim: Fixed constraints: no webhooks reach the box so GitHub is polled; 20 runner slots (314(b)); agents crash, stall and mis-report; the owner is asked rarely and well

R10.claim: Compensating mechanisms 20 today, target under 5; clocks 5 to 1; stores of work state 4 to 1 plus the task file as the owner's view

R13.claim: The scheduler is a pure function run on every event, never sleeps; the reconciler is the only clock, a GitHub poller (30-60 s, ETags), a backstop
